name: GOLIATH
question: Is 180-W GreenLight XPS laser vaporization of the prostate noninferior to TURP for symptom relief, flow and complications in men with benign prostatic obstruction?

arms.label: 180-W GreenLight XPS laser photoselective vaporization of the prostate
monopolar or bipolar transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP)

design.population: Men aged 40 to 80 years with benign prostatic obstruction (IPSS 12 or higher, Qmax below 15 mL/s, prostate 100 g or less on transrectal ultrasound); 281 were randomized and 269 treated.
design.locator: Abstracts of the 6-, 12- and 24-month reports (281 randomized, 269 treated, 29 centers, 9 countries); randomized arm sizes (139 and 142), age limits and eligibility from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01218672 participant flow and eligibility fields

verdictNote: Noninferior to TURP on IPSS, Qmax and complication-free rate at 6 months, sustained through 24 months
takeaway: In 281 men with benign prostatic obstruction and prostates up to 100 g, 180-W GreenLight XPS laser vaporization was noninferior to TURP for 6-month IPSS, Qmax and complication-free proportion, with shorter catheterization and hospital stay.

reports.label: 6-month safety and efficacy
reports.citation: Bachmann A, Tubaro A, Barber N, et al. "180-W XPS GreenLight Laser Vaporisation Versus Transurethral Resection of the Prostate for the Treatment of Benign Prostatic Obstruction: 6-Month Safety and Efficacy Results of a European Multicentre Randomised Trial—The GOLIATH Study." *Eur Urol.* 2014;65(5):931-942. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.10.040

results.measure: Mean IPSS at 6 months (lower is better; laser minus TURP)
results.note: Abstract: noninferiority of XPS to TURP for IPSS demonstrated (one-sided tests at the 2.5% level); the margin was 3 IPSS points. Means are from 134 laser and 131 TURP patients analyzed; difference by subtraction.
results.locator: Abstract (noninferiority); means, SD (5.2 and 4.9) and denominators from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01218672 posted results, primary outcome; margin from the 24-month report abstract

results.measure: Mean maximum flow rate at 6 months, mL/s (laser minus TURP)
results.note: Abstract: noninferiority demonstrated for Qmax (margin 5 mL/s). Means (SD 10.1 and 11.4) and difference as printed in Table 3.

results.measure: Proportion free of device- or procedure-related complications through 180 days (laser minus TURP)
results.note: Abstract: noninferiority demonstrated for the complication-free proportion (margin 5%). 117 of 134 laser and 109 of 131 TURP patients; difference in percentage points as printed in Table 3. Registry definition: perforation, prolonged or secondary hospitalization, or a surgical or invasive intervention, excluding catheterization for transient retention under 7 days.
results.locator: Abstract (noninferiority); Table 3, complication free during 180 days; definition from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01218672 posted results

results.note: Abstract: the early reintervention rate was three times higher after TURP; overall postoperative reintervention rates did not differ significantly between arms at 6 months.

results.measure: Time until stable health status, length of catheterization and length of hospital stay
results.note: Abstract: all three were superior with XPS. Median values are under treatment delivery facts.
